correctness.rationale: The exact one-grain overwrite channel preserves first physical coordinate; global bit complement conjugates the two 64-vertex branches. Error-ball intersections induce a branch compatibility graph with 1584 edges and 432 incompatibility edges. Independently reconstructed the branch graph from direct overwrite balls and used NetworkX maximal-clique enumeration of all 118772 maximal cliques: unique largest clique has 13 vertices, exactly (0,3,6,9,21,28,31,42,45,48,51,54,57), no 14-clique. Thus there is one size-13 code in each branch and exactly one labeled full size-26 union; complements and all its pairwise ball disjointness follow. The pinned verifier also contains two formally exhaustive recursive searches; the independent maximal-clique enumeration is a separate exact finite check. No general n claim.

originality.rationale: Sharov–Roth already establish M(7,1)=26, cited in Gabrys–Yaakobi–Dolecek Table II. Their uniqueness results concern unlimited grain errors or odd n at t=(n−3)/2 (t=2 for n=7), not the present t=1 equality classification. Resultary has a separate complete maximum single-grain code census for n=6; that does not fix the 64-vertex branch optimizer at n=7. Exact sole labeled optimum for n7 t1 is the surviving novelty; Sharov–Roth original full paper remained access-limited, a material priority risk.
